Gold Analysis (XAU/USD)

Fundamental Overview

Gold price dropped below the psychological $3,300 level during the Asian session. The decline was driven by the ongoing truce between Iran and Israel, which has weakened demand for safe-haven assets. Additional pressure on the precious metal came from reports of a trade agreement between the US and China, boosting risk-on sentiment.

Investor focus now shifts to today’s release of the Fed’s preferred inflation measure – the PCE Price Index. A monthly increase of 0.1% is expected, while annual figures are forecasted at 2.3% (headline) and 2.6% (core), both above last year’s levels.

Fed Chair Jerome Powell reiterated a cautious stance on rate cuts during his testimony in Congress this week, warning that tariff-driven inflation might be more persistent than initially anticipated. Meanwhile, President Trump increased pressure on Powell, stating he is considering several candidates to replace him, with an announcement possibly coming as early as September.

⸻

Technical Analysis
 • Resistances: 3,336, 3,350, 3,370
 • Supports: 3,271, 3,250, 3,232

⸻

Conclusion

Gold dropped below $3,300 due to easing geopolitical tensions and positive news on US-China trade relations. If today’s PCE data exceeds expectations, further downside may be seen below the 3,271 support, with the next target at 3,250. Conversely, weaker inflation data could weaken the dollar and help gold rebound toward the 3,336 resistance, and if broken, extend gains to 3,350 or even 3,370. Markets will be highly sensitive to today’s US inflation release.

$50 Short & the Gold $3000 sell-off continues - no war doesn't drive gold.

Structure expectadley failed at 3337, adding more positions, which retested into Asia to London and NYC which and Gold broke down with volume expansion, and USD decoupling

Friday Watchlist:
Core PCE at 13:30 UK

DXY bounce likely = gold pressure
